Split photos into training and test sets by observation

Source: R/benchmark.R
splitByObservation.Rd

Photos of one observation show the same individual, often seconds apart. Putting one in the training set and another in the test set would make a key look better than it is, so whole observations go to one side.

Usage

splitByObservation(observation, label, test = 0.3, seed = 1)

Arguments

observation

The observation each photo belongs to. A photo without one (NA) counts as an observation of its own.

label

The class of each photo. The split is made within each class, so every class keeps about the same share for testing.

test

Share of each class's observations to test with.

seed

Seed for the draw.

Value

A character vector, "train" or "test" for each photo. A class with two or more observations gets at least one on each side; a class with a single observation goes to the training set. An observation with photos in several classes stays whole too: all its photos go to the training set, so nothing in the test set has a sibling in training.

Examples

obs <- c(1, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 5, 6)
label <- rep(c("oak", "elm"), each = 4)
data.frame(obs, label, split = splitByObservation(obs, label, test = 0.5))
#>   obs label split
#> 1   1   oak  test
#> 2   1   oak  test
#> 3   2   oak train
#> 4   3   oak  test
#> 5   4   elm  test
#> 6   5   elm  test
#> 7   5   elm  test
#> 8   6   elm train
